title: Gummy hands: search for hidden alternatives
context: Age approximately two; children guess location of gummy after some manipulated rounds
information_available: Visible fist positions, previous outcomes across neighboring children, no external access to game design
perceived_objective: Find the gummy and understand why outcomes shift
observed_actions: Observes neighboring trials, considers a third location behind instructor even after counterexamples, guesses behind twice
observed_result: Both novel third-option guesses are WRONG in presented trials; adults remark on hypothesis-generation rather than accuracy
epistemic_limits: Do not code perfect deduction, mind-reading or successful inference; later description is retrospective narration
alternate_outcomes_to_test: Instructor conceals gummy outside both hands vs places it inside hand; vary peer observation and instructor cues.
memory_seed_policy: Never import the canonical episode as an occurrence after a simulation divergence; pre-existing skills may be used only in character-behavioral calibration
